prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro: urban CBTC railway (peak/off-peak/engineering hours); CBTC handles separation, movement authority (MA), regulation. Actors: Line Traffic Controller (monitors, incidents, uses Lantern; regulating requests executed only if interlocking and CBTC rules agree route safe; no vital intervention); Revenue Train Operator (cab; acknowledgements to Atlas via monitored path); field staff; Signal Maintenance Engineer, alias Maple (uses Maintenance Diagnostic Server; verifies and records track clearance evidence before restoring normal route setting after detection anomaly); Cyber Security Officer (access, keys). Elements: - Metro Operations Control System, alias Lantern: regulation, alarms, commands; displays commanded route, locked route, point state, occupancy, zone/radio/supervision states separately; sends Crew Login Token Bundle to Atlas. - North District Zone Controller, alias Marble (north, East Junction routes only if consistent with MA). South District Zone Controller, alias Orchid (south, West Junction, flank, conflict locking). Both send MA onboard; receiving zone validates route, train identity, boundary section before extending. Route enters MA only after overlap/flank protected; point correspondence loss shortens/withdraws MA per braking envelope; release exception is retained hazard until path excluded. - East Junction Interlocking, alias Falcon (sends Axle Counter Reset Request in degraded-mode procedure; reset inhibited while route locked or train approaching); West Junction Interlocking (sends Route Release Exception List when sectional release times out). Both report points, occupancy, locking via vital interfaces; final authority over points, locking, release; route needs points detected, locked, proved. - Axle counters: independent evidence; conflict with CBTC location applies more restrictive state. - Wayside supervision: mismatch withholds/shortens MA. - Atlas Onboard Controller, alias Kestrel: ATP, MA, speed, doors; modes initialization, protected manual, ATO, fallback, cutout; validates context via token bundle; produces Brake Curve Checksum Log; confirms position from Dual Channel Odometer (divergence degrades mode) at boundary; radio loss uses last validated MA. - Train Radio Modem: via Wayside Radio Access Network, alias Saffron (make-before-break, sequence/timeout monitoring; sends Radio Handover Audit File). - Safety Data Communication Network: authenticated, deterministic vital delivery; sends Clock Drift Sample Report. - Cryptographic Key Management Appliance. - Maintenance Diagnostic Server: records health, route outcomes, point timing, detection; non-vital. - Service Timetable

New part:
S101: The Operations Control Centre workflow begins with the Line Traffic Controller maintaining a live view of train positions, route status, alarms, and service performance across the Greenvale Metro line.
S102: The Metro Operations Control System presents regulating options based on timetable variance, platform dwell time, headway spacing, and the current availability of routes.
S103: The Line Traffic Controller selects holding, skip-stop, turnback, or run-through measures only after checking that passenger impact and downstream recovery have been assessed.
S104: Lantern displays the proposed regulating action, affected train identities, and predicted recovery time before the Line Traffic Controller confirms the command.
S105: The North District Zone Controller applies movement authority constraints according to the confirmed operating state and reports any conflict or unavailable route condition for controller review.
S106: The South District Zone Controller applies the same operating principles for the southern section while preserving separation margins and route locking conditions.
S107: East Junction Interlocking holds the route locked until track section detection, point correspondence, and opposing route conditions meet the configured release criteria.
S108: West Junction Interlocking provides route state indications that allow the Operations Control Centre to distinguish an operational delay from a signalling equipment fault.
S109: When an engineering possession or field report requires a temporary operating constraint, the Line Traffic Controller produces the Temporary Speed Restriction Notice after confirming the limits, speed value, start time, and expected removal condition.
S110: After a temporary operating constraint is active, the Line Traffic Controller monitors actual train performance against the expected delay allowance and adjusts regulation plans when recovery margins are exceeded.
S111: The Atlas Onboard Controller enforces the active movement profile on each equipped train and presents any onboard rejection or degraded mode indication for operational assessment.
S112: The Dual Channel Odometer supports train position confidence by providing independent distance measurement inputs that are considered during degraded operation review.
S113: The Train Radio Modem supports continuous operational messaging, and loss of radio availability is treated as a service risk that may require holding trains before constrained areas.
S114: The Wayside Radio Access Network is monitored for coverage alarms, handover irregularities, and capacity conditions that could affect the stability of train control communications.
S115: The Safety Data Communication Network is monitored as a safety-related bearer, and persistent communication faults are escalated before additional regulating actions are attempted in the affected area.
S116: For incident management, the Line Traffic Controller records the initial event time, train identifier, location, passenger impact, and the first safe operating instruction issued.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
